question: Can a child lead the taraweeh prayer at home?
answer:
Also realize as well that leading the taraweeh prayer: the taraweeh is a nafil salah, and so firstly, according to most of the madhhabs, a child can lead the nafil salah. Some of the madhhabs have been stricter and said that for the fard salah you cannot have a child lead.

Child meaning what is *mumayyiz*. So there's *ghayr baligh*: there's a child that's a toddler, and then there's a child that is of *sinn al-tamyiz*. And mumayyiz means they can understand. Like, imagine a seven-year-old. The average seven-year-old understands: I need to do wudu, I cannot break my wudu, I have to pray in a proper manner. A two-year-old would not understand these things. So obviously a toddler is too young to lead anything.

But there's something called sinn al-tamyiz, and tamyiz is that a child understands, is cognizant. Definitely the few years before puberty (so puberty, let's say it's 12 years old, 13 years old), definitely the 10-year-old, the 9-year-old, is old enough to understand what is haram and halal, what breaks wudu, to go and do wudu again. That is called sinn al-tamyiz. When does it begin? It varies from child to child. There are some children at the age of 5 who fully understand. The point being, you want somebody who knows how to do wudu, and who knows when wudu breaks, and who knows to pray salah in a serious manner. That is called sinn al-tamyiz.

**And since taraweeh is a nafil salah, it is not a fard salah, therefore you can have a child lead, by all of the four madhhabs, no problem.** You can have a child lead. Why do I say this? Because in many households some of our children have memorized more Qur'an than us. Some of our children are going to the tahfiz school, and they've, alhamdulillah, done five, 10, 15 juz' with better tajweed than the parents. And so this is a good opportunity to encourage these youngsters to lead the salah.

Now, a girl can only lead other females in salah. And so if you have a hafidhah, or a young girl that is doing hifz, she may take her mother and her sisters and she may lead them in the salah, no problem. And she will stand in the same row as them, not in front of them. And a boy can lead both boys and girls in the salah.

And this is something that is well known. There's a famous hadith of Amr ibn Salamah. It's actually a little bit funny in its own way. It's a very beautiful hadith, it is in Sahih Bukhari; it's very long, so I'm going to summarize it in my own words. Amr ibn Salamah says that I was a young boy, you know, six, seven years old, and the tribes would go back and forth in our village, and we heard of Islam that way. We were not in Medina; he's in a small village, and they heard of Islam that way. And these tribes, the Muslims, would come in and out, and I started memorizing the Qur'an from them when they're going through and back and forth. Because I was the youngest, I had a good memory; I memorized the Qur'an even not as a Muslim.

Eventually my father accepted Islam after the conquest of Mecca, and my father went to the Prophet ﷺ in Medina. He came back with this commandment: that at every time of the salah the adhan should be given, and then the one amongst you who knows the most Qur'an should be the imam. So Amr says that they looked around, they did an exam, they quizzed everybody, and they discovered I knew the most Qur'an, because I was memorizing from the travellers. And these are all new Muslims now, the tribe, but since he used to interact with the Muslim community, since he would sit with them and listen, look at them pray, he memorized surahs from the Qur'an. So he said they found me to be the one who knew the most Qur'an, even though I was six or seven years old at the time, so they made me their imam.

And I was a poor child. I didn't even have full clothes. I just had an upper garment that would come on top of me, and when I would go into sajdah my back would be exposed, because he was poor. He didn't even know he should have actually put it on his waist, but he doesn't know, he's a child anyway, he's a six-, seven-year-old. And so I went into sajdah, and my back (I mean literally the back, you know what I'm talking about) was exposed. And so a lady screamed out from the back and she said, "O people, cover the behind of your imam!" Some lady screamed out, "Cover the behind of your imam!" And so the men came together after the salah, and they purchased for me a brand new cloak. Amr says it was the happiest day of my life at that time, and I was only six or seven years old.

Now, the hadith is very nice and cute and funny and whatnot, but what it shows us is that Amr, during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, this is happening, Amr would lead his tribe in salah, because they didn't know any Qur'an and he had already memorized a few surahs, and so they made him their imam. I'm just mentioning that on the side.

The point being that, for pretty much all of them, there is no issue with a child leading the salah, as long as the child understands the rulings of salah. And what that means is that, in particular, there should be an element of seriousness. The child should not be joking and laughing. There should be a cognizance, an awareness of wudu and of what breaks wudu, and the arkan of prayer, and even the basics of sajdah. So at least teach them, even at that time, and then he may lead the family in salah, no problem.
